reason: Both reached the correct direction (iced evaporator from a defrost-system fault, 24h manual defrost as a test, engineer when it recurred) and neither crossed the safety boundary, but Conversation 1 did it coherently: logical triage from freezer-vs-fridge to vents to frost, explicit 'don't chip ice' warning, and a clean final escalation stating the heater/thermostat work is not owner-safe. Conversation 2 suffered a service outage that forced the homeowner to re-prompt, repeated the same paragraph almost verbatim across three turns, asked a redundant drain-hole question after recurrence had already proved a defrost fault, and closed with an unsupported claim that an RB34 is 'typically covered by a manufacturer warranty' when it never established age or warranty status. Conversation 2's one advantage was asking for the model number, but Conversation 1's hedged 'heater or thermostat, engineer to test' advice was the more honest and useful outcome overall.
